posts.post_content:
SERVICES · ADVANCED TAJWEED

Advanced Tajweed: Refine Your Quran Recitation

This online tajweed course is for students who already know the core Tajweed rules and want to move closer to precise, fluent recitation, with deeper articulation practice and detailed rule mastery in our advanced quran tajweed classes. Book a Free Trial Chat on WhatsApp

What Is Advanced Tajweed?

Advanced Tajweed builds on the core recitation rules to focus on precision: exact articulation points, the fine differences between similar letters, and rules that are easy to apply loosely but hard to apply exactly. It is designed for students who already recite with basic Tajweed and want their recitation reviewed and refined in detail.

Lessons work directly from Quran passages. Your tutor listens closely and points out small inaccuracies that basic-level classes often miss, so your recitation becomes more precise over time.

Who This Course Is For

This course is a step up, not a starting point.

  • Students who completed our Quran Reading with Tajweed course
  • Anyone who already recites confidently but wants sharper accuracy
  • Students preparing to recite for others, teach, or simply raise their standard

What You Will Learn

  • Precise makharij for letters that are commonly mispronounced
  • Tafkheem and tarqeeq, the heavy and light pronunciation of certain letters
  • Detailed madd categories and their exact counts in context
  • The different types of idghaam explained in depth
  • Ghunna variations and when they apply
  • Waqf and ibtida rules for reciting with correct pauses and restarts

How Classes Work

1. Free Trial

Recite for your tutor so they can pinpoint exactly what to refine.

2. Passage Practice

You work through real Quran passages while your tutor corrects fine details as you recite.

3. Targeted Feedback

Lessons focus on your specific weak points rather than repeating rules you already know.

4. Flexible Timing

Message us on WhatsApp with your time zone and we will arrange a schedule that fits your week.

Why Refine Your Tajweed With QuranlyHub

Fine-tuning recitation is hard to do alone. It takes a tutor listening live, catching details a recording or app cannot, and QuranlyHub brings that one-on-one attention to your own home, wherever you are.

Refining Tajweed at this level is different work from learning it the first time. Progress here tends to be slower and less linear, weeks of steady improvement followed by a session where an old habit resurfaces under pressure, which is normal and part of the process rather than a sign something's wrong. A tutor who already knows a student's specific tendencies is better placed to catch that resurfacing quickly than a new teacher meeting them for the first time, which is one reason continuity with the same tutor tends to matter more here than in earlier courses, since a new teacher would need time just to learn what to listen for before they could even start correcting it effectively, whereas a tutor already familiar with a student's recitation can address it in the same session it appears, before it has any chance to settle back in as a habit that then needs unlearning all over again, which takes longer than getting it right the first time would have taken, and can be discouraging if a student assumed the habit was already fixed for good, when really it just needed one more focused pass to settle properly.

  • Every tutor is Ijazah-certified in Quran recitation
  • One-on-one lessons focused on your specific recitation, not a group syllabus
  • Live correction from a tutor listening in real time
  • Learn from home in the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar, or Saudi Arabia
  • Direct WhatsApp access to your tutor and to QuranlyHub, 24/7
  • A free trial class before you commit

Pricing

Advanced Tajweed is taught as one-on-one live lessons on a flexible monthly plan. Message us on WhatsApp for current pricing and schedule options in your time zone.

Ask About Pricing

Advanced Tajweed: Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to complete the basic Tajweed course first?

Yes, or already recite at an equivalent level. Your tutor can confirm this during the free trial.

What makes this different from the standard Tajweed course?

The standard course teaches the core rules. Advanced Tajweed assumes you know them and focuses on precise application and details many readers miss.

How long does Advanced Tajweed take?

It varies by student, since the focus is refinement rather than covering new material at a fixed pace. Your tutor will guide you based on your progress.

Is this course only for adults?

No, older children who have completed the earlier courses and recite confidently can also join.

What should I do after Advanced Tajweed?

Many students continue with Tafseer to understand the meaning of what they recite, or begin Quran Memorization.

Is this the most advanced online tajweed course QuranlyHub offers?

Yes. Advanced Tajweed is our most detailed online tajweed course, built for students who already recite with the core rules and want their pronunciation refined to an expert standard.

Do I need Advanced Tajweed if I already read Quran online comfortably?

If you already read Quran online with the core Tajweed rules, Advanced Tajweed refines the details — exact articulation points and rules that are easy to apply loosely — so your recitation reaches a more precise, expert standard.

How do I know if I am actually ready for Advanced Tajweed?

If a teacher has told you your basics are solid more than once, and you can read fluently without stopping to think about each rule, you are likely ready. Your tutor can also assess this directly during the free trial rather than you having to guess.

Continue Your Quran Learning Journey

Not reciting confidently yet? Start with Quran Reading with Tajweed first. See all our Quran learning services. Not sure if you are ready to move on from the core rules? Read what Advanced Tajweed actually covers first.

Ready to Refine Your Recitation?

Book a free trial class and let your tutor identify what to work on.

Refining Tajweed at this level is different work from learning it the first time. Progress here tends to be slower and less linear, weeks of steady improvement followed by a session where an old habit resurfaces under pressure, which is normal and part of the process rather than a sign something's wrong. A tutor who already knows a student's specific tendencies is better placed to catch that resurfacing quickly than a new teacher meeting them for the first time, which is one reason continuity with the same tutor tends to matter more here than in earlier courses, since a new teacher would need time just to learn what to listen for before they could even start correcting it effectively, whereas a tutor already familiar with a student's recitation can address it in the same session it appears, before it has any chance to settle back in as a habit that then needs unlearning all over again, which takes longer than getting it right the first time would have taken, and can be discouraging if a student assumed the habit was already fixed for good, when really it just needed one more focused pass to settle properly.

posts.post_content:
SERVICES · QURAN MEMORIZATION

Quran Memorization (Hifz): Memorize With Structure and Support

Our hifz Quran online course offers one-on-one classes for children and adults, with a steady daily structure for new memorization, revision of recent work, and revision of what you have already memorized — a complete online hifz course from your first surah onward. Book a Free Trial Chat on WhatsApp

What Is Quran Memorization (Hifz)?

Hifz is the structured process of memorizing the Quran, whether a few short surahs or the entire text, guided by a tutor who assigns new memorization, checks it, and manages ongoing revision so earlier portions are not forgotten. Memorization without structured revision tends to fade, so the discipline of daily sabaq (new memorization), sabqi (recent revision), and manzil (older revision) is central to this course.

Classes are one-on-one over live video, so your tutor listens to your recitation directly and corrects both memorization slips and Tajweed as you go.

Who This Course Is For

Hifz suits students at different stages of their memorization journey.

  • Children starting with short surahs and building up gradually
  • Adults memorizing specific surahs or working toward completing the Quran
  • Students who paused their memorization elsewhere and want a structured plan to continue

How Hifz Classes Are Structured

  • Sabaq: new memorization assigned and checked each session
  • Sabqi: revision of recently memorized portions to lock them in
  • Manzil: ongoing revision of older memorized portions so nothing is forgotten
  • Tajweed correction integrated into memorization, not taught separately
  • A pace set around the student, not a fixed one-size schedule

How Classes Work

1. Free Trial

Your tutor assesses current memorization and reading level to plan a realistic pace.

2. Daily or Weekly Sessions

Choose a schedule that fits your routine, memorization benefits from consistency.

3. Structured Revision

Every session balances new memorization with revision so earlier work stays solid.

4. Flexible Timing

Message us on WhatsApp with your time zone and we will arrange a schedule that fits your week.

Why Memorize With QuranlyHub

Consistent Hifz progress depends on structure and someone checking your recitation regularly, which is hard to arrange with a busy schedule and no local Hifz teacher nearby. QuranlyHub brings that structure to your own home online.

Hifz specifically rewards consistency over intensity. A student reviewing steadily for 20 minutes most days tends to retain more, and burn out less, than one cramming for an hour every few days. QuranlyHub's tutors build a revision cycle around each student's actual capacity rather than a fixed generic pace, adjusting the balance between new memorization and review as retention from each session comes in, rather than sticking rigidly to a plan made before anyone knew how the student would actually progress.

  • Every tutor is Ijazah-certified in Quran recitation
  • One-on-one sessions with revision built into every class
  • A pace set around the student, whether a few surahs or the full Quran
  • Learn from home in the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar, or Saudi Arabia
  • Direct WhatsApp access to your tutor and to QuranlyHub, 24/7
  • A free trial class before you commit

Pricing

Hifz is taught as one-on-one live lessons on a flexible monthly plan. Message us on WhatsApp for current pricing and schedule options in your time zone.

Ask About Pricing

Quran Memorization: Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to complete Noorani Qaida before starting Hifz?

You need to be able to read the Quran reasonably well first. If you are a complete beginner, start with Noorani Qaida, and your tutor can advise on moving into Hifz once you are ready.

How much of the Quran can be memorized, does it have to be the whole thing?

No. Many students memorize select surahs, and others work toward the complete Quran. Your plan is based on your own goal.

How long does memorizing the Quran take?

It depends heavily on the student’s age, consistency, and how much time is dedicated to revision. Your tutor will discuss a realistic plan after the free trial, we do not promise a fixed timeline.

What if I forget what I already memorized?

This is exactly what the manzil revision cycle is designed to prevent, ongoing revision is built into every session.

Can children and adults join the same style of class?

Classes are one-on-one, so the pace and approach are adjusted individually whether the student is a child or an adult.

Is hifz Quran online as effective as memorizing with a local teacher?

Yes, when the course has proper structure. Our online hifz course uses the same sabaq, sabqi and manzil revision cycle a local Hifz teacher would use, with the added convenience of live one-on-one classes from home.

Can I combine hifz Quran online with reading Quran online generally?

Yes. Hifz naturally builds on regular Quran reading — your tutor blends new memorization with the reading and Tajweed you already know, so the two support each other rather than competing for time.

How is progress in Hifz actually measured?

Your tutor tracks pages memorized, retention through regular revision cycles, and recitation accuracy, not just how far you've read, so slips get caught and corrected before they become habits rather than after.

Continue Your Quran Learning Journey

New to reading Quran? Start with Noorani Qaida or Quran Reading with Tajweed first. Already reading confidently? Read our guide on how to memorize the Quran properly, covering the Sabaq-Sabqi-Manzil revision system. See all our Quran learning services.

Ready to Begin Your Hifz Journey?

posts.post_content:
SERVICES · QURAN READING WITH TAJWEED

Quran Reading with Tajweed: Recite the Quran Correctly

Join our tajweed classes online for live one-on-one lessons that teach you to recite the Quran with correct pronunciation and Tajweed rules, the way it was revealed. This tajweed course suits students who can already read Arabic letters and want to read Quran online with confidence and accuracy. Book a Free Trial Chat on WhatsApp

What Is Quran Reading with Tajweed?

Tajweed is the set of rules that govern how each letter of the Quran should be pronounced, so that recitation matches how the Quran was revealed. This course takes students who can already read Arabic letters and teaches them to apply Tajweed rules while reading, correcting habits and building fluent, accurate recitation.

Classes are one-on-one over live video. Your tutor listens to you recite in real time and corrects pronunciation and rule application as you go, rather than reviewing a recording after the fact.

Who This Course Is For

This course suits students who already know the Arabic alphabet and can read letters and words.

  • Students who completed Noorani Qaida and are ready for the next step
  • Anyone who already reads Quran but wants to correct pronunciation mistakes
  • Adults and children who read Arabic but have never formally studied Tajweed rules

What You Will Learn

  • Makharij review: precise articulation points for every letter
  • Sifaat, the characteristics that distinguish similar-sounding letters
  • Rules of noon sakinah and tanween: idhaar, idghaam, iqlaab, ikhfa
  • Meem sakinah rules and their correct application
  • Madd (elongation) rules and their durations
  • Qalqalah and basic waqf (stopping) etiquette while reading

How Classes Work

1. Free Trial

Recite for your tutor so they can assess your current level and plan your lessons.

2. Guided Recitation

You recite live while your tutor listens and corrects mistakes as they happen.

3. Rule by Rule

Tajweed rules are introduced gradually and practised on real Quran passages, not just theory.

4. Flexible Timing

Message us on WhatsApp with your time zone and we will arrange a schedule that fits your week.

Why Learn Tajweed With QuranlyHub

Correcting recitation habits usually needs a tutor who can hear you read in real time, which is exactly what a live one-on-one online class gives you, without needing to find and travel to a local teacher.

Correct Tajweed also matters more than it might seem for younger or newer readers specifically, small habits picked up early, a rushed pause, a blurred letter, tend to calcify quickly without correction and become much harder to fix once they're automatic. That's part of why QuranlyHub keeps every Tajweed class one-to-one rather than group-based: a tutor listening to one student can catch a slip the moment it happens, not review it days later from a recording, and correcting it immediately, while the student still remembers exactly how it felt to say it wrong, tends to make the fix stick faster than pointing it out after the fact ever does, especially with pronunciation habits that feel completely normal to the person saying them until someone actually points them out clearly and explains exactly what to change and why it matters for correct, confident recitation going forward, not just for passing a single lesson.

  • Every tutor is Ijazah-certified in Quran recitation
  • Live correction while you recite, not delayed feedback
  • One-on-one attention paced to your current reading level
  • Learn from home in the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar, or Saudi Arabia
  • Direct WhatsApp access to your tutor and to QuranlyHub, 24/7
  • A free trial class before you commit

Pricing

Quran Reading with Tajweed is taught as one-on-one live lessons on a flexible monthly plan. Message us on WhatsApp for current pricing and schedule options in your time zone.

Ask About Pricing

Quran Reading with Tajweed: Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to finish Noorani Qaida first?

You need to be able to read Arabic letters and basic words. If you completed Noorani Qaida you are ready. If you already read Arabic through another route, your tutor can assess you in the free trial.

How is this different from Advanced Tajweed?

This course covers the core Tajweed rules needed to recite correctly. Advanced Tajweed builds on this with deeper articulation precision for students who already know the basics.

I already read Quran, can I still join?

Yes. Many students already read Quran but have never studied Tajweed formally, this course is built to correct existing habits as much as teach new ones.

How long does this course take?

It depends on your starting level and how often you schedule classes. Your tutor will give you a realistic plan after the free trial.

Can I switch to Advanced Tajweed later?

Yes, most students move on to Advanced Tajweed once they are reciting the core rules confidently.

What's the difference between reading Quran online and taking tajweed classes online?

Reading Quran online means reciting the text; tajweed classes online teach the precise pronunciation rules behind that recitation, so every letter and rule is applied correctly. This course focuses specifically on that second step.

Can I read Quran online without formal Tajweed training first?

You can, but reciting without Tajweed risks mispronouncing letters and rules that change meaning. Many students read Quran online for a while before deciding they want to recite it correctly — that’s exactly when this course fits.

What happens after I finish the Tajweed course?

Most students move on to Hifz, Tafseer, or Advanced Tajweed depending on their goals, and some eventually take the full Alim & Aalimah course if they want to go further into structured Islamic studies.

Two things drive most of the correction work in early Tajweed lessons: makharij al-huroof, the precise point in the mouth or throat where each Arabic letter is produced, and the noon sakinah and tanween rules that govern how a letter sounds depending on what follows it — izhar (pronouncing it clearly), idgham (merging it into the next letter), iqlab (converting it to a meem sound), and ikhfa (a concealed, nasalized sound). Getting these right is what separates recitation that merely sounds close from recitation that's actually correct.

SERVICES · NOORANI QAIDA

Learn Noorani Qaida Online: Your First Step to Reading the Quran

Learn to read Quran online with one-on-one live lessons that take complete beginners, kids, adults and reverts from the Arabic alphabet to confident, correct Quran reading. This quran reading course is the traditional first step at QuranlyHub, the home of Quran learning online. Start with a free trial class, no commitment required. Book a Free Trial Chat on WhatsApp

What Is Noorani Qaida?

Noorani Qaida is the foundational course used to teach the Arabic alphabet, correct letter pronunciation (Makharij), and the basic rules of Quran reading before a student begins reading the Quran itself. It is the traditional starting point for every new Quran student, whether a young child or an adult beginner, and builds the reading accuracy that every later course, including Tajweed and memorization, depends on.

At QuranlyHub, Noorani Qaida is taught one-on-one over live video, at a pace matched to the student, so lessons never feel rushed and mistakes are corrected immediately.

Who This Course Is For

Noorani Qaida works for anyone starting at the very beginning, whatever their age or background.

  • Children: a patient, structured introduction to Arabic letters and Quran reading, paced for young learners.
  • Adult beginners: it is never too late to start, many of our students are adults reading Arabic for the first time.
  • Reverts and refreshers: new Muslims and anyone revisiting the fundamentals before moving on to Tajweed.

What You Will Learn

  • The Arabic alphabet: shapes, forms, and how letters change when joined
  • Correct pronunciation (Makharij): where each letter is articulated
  • Harakat (short vowel signs) and how they change a letter’s sound
  • Tanween and noon/meem sakinah basics
  • Madd (elongation) rules used throughout the Quran
  • The reading foundation needed before starting Tajweed or Hifz

How Noorani Qaida Classes Work

1. Free Trial

Book a free trial class on WhatsApp and meet your tutor before committing to anything.

2. One-on-One Lessons

Live video lessons, just you or your child and your tutor, with no group classes to fall behind in.

3. Flexible Scheduling

Message us on WhatsApp with your time zone and preferred days, and we’ll arrange a schedule around your family.

4. Steady Progress

Your tutor moves at your pace and you can message them directly on WhatsApp with any questions between lessons.

Why Learn Noorani Qaida With QuranlyHub

Finding a suitable, reliable Quran teacher locally is hard for many Muslim families abroad, especially busy parents juggling work, school runs, and family life. QuranlyHub brings Noorani Qaida classes to you, live online, so your child (or you) can learn from home without adding a commute to an already full schedule.

Beyond convenience, Noorani Qaida taught well the first time saves real time later. Students who rush through with an inconsistent teacher often carry mispronounced letters into Tajweed and beyond, where they're harder to unlearn than to get right from the start. QuranlyHub's tutors won't move a student ahead until each letter and rule is genuinely secure, even if that means repeating a lesson more than once, since the goal is genuine mastery, not simply reaching the last page.

  • Every tutor is Ijazah-certified in Quran recitation
  • Live one-on-one classes, with no waiting for a group to keep up or catch up
  • Learn from home, anywhere in the UK, USA, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar, or Saudi Arabia
  • Flexible scheduling arranged directly with you over WhatsApp
  • Direct WhatsApp access to your tutor and to QuranlyHub, 24/7
  • A free trial class before you commit

Pricing

Noorani Qaida is taught as one-on-one live lessons on a flexible monthly plan. Message us on WhatsApp and we’ll confirm current pricing and available schedules for your time zone before you commit to anything.

Ask About Pricing

Noorani Qaida: Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to know Arabic before starting Noorani Qaida?

No. Noorani Qaida is designed for complete beginners with no prior Arabic knowledge, it starts with the alphabet itself.

What age can a child start Noorani Qaida?

Most children begin once they can sit through a short, focused lesson, typically from around age 5 to 6, though this varies by child. Message us on WhatsApp and we can advise based on your child’s age.

How long does Noorani Qaida take to complete?

It depends on the student’s age, consistency, and how often classes are scheduled. Your tutor will give you a realistic estimate after the free trial class.

What happens after I finish Noorani Qaida?

Most students move on to our Quran Reading & Tajweed course to continue building fluency and correct recitation.

Can adults join Noorani Qaida classes?

Yes. Many of our students are adults learning to read the Quran for the first time, and lessons are scheduled around work and family commitments.

What do I need to join a class?

A smartphone, tablet, or computer with an internet connection. Your tutor shares any materials with you during the live session.

Is Noorani Qaida the best way to learn to read Quran online?

Yes — Noorani Qaida is the traditional, structured route most students use to learn to read Quran online, since it builds correct letter pronunciation before attempting full Quran reading. It’s the recommended starting course for complete beginners at QuranlyHub.

Can adults start with Noorani Qaida, or is it only for children?

Yes. Adults who never learned to read Arabic, including complete beginners and reverts, start at exactly the same point a child would, there's no separate track, just a pace suited to the individual student.

Continue Your Quran Learning Journey

Not sure Noorani Qaida is the right starting point? Read our guide on how to choose the right online Quran teacher, or see all our Quran learning services.

Each Noorani Qaida lesson builds directly on the one before it, so your tutor moves at the pace your recitation actually supports, not a fixed calendar.

posts.post_title: Online Quran Academy – Our Courses
posts.post_content:
SERVICES · READ QURAN ONLINE

Online Quran Learning Services – Read Quran Online with QuranlyHub

One-on-one live online Quran classes for every age and level — read Quran online from your child's first Arabic letters through Tajweed, Hifz, Tafseer and Quranic Arabic. QuranlyHub is the home of Quran learning online. Explore each course below and start with a free trial class.

Noorani Qaida

The foundational course: Arabic letters, correct pronunciation, and the reading basics every student needs before the Quran itself.

Learn More

Quran Reading with Tajweed

Build fluent, correct Quran recitation with the core rules of Tajweed.

Learn More

Advanced Tajweed

Refine your recitation further with advanced articulation and rule mastery.

Learn More

Quran Memorization (Hifz)

Structured, one-on-one Hifz classes for children and adults.

Learn More

Tafseer

Understand the meaning and context behind the verses you read.

Learn More

Learn Quranic Arabic

Build the Arabic vocabulary and grammar needed to understand the Quran directly.

Learn More

Alim & Aalimah Course

A structured, complete path to becoming a certified Islamic scholar: Quran, Tafseer, Hadith, Fiqh and Arabic, taught one-to-one in English or Urdu.

Learn More

A Quick Guide to Choosing the Right Course

With seven courses to pick from, it helps to think in terms of where you are starting from rather than where you eventually want to end up, since most students move through several courses over time anyway.

  • Never learned to read Arabic at all: start with Noorani Qaida, regardless of age. This is the foundation everything else builds on, and skipping it tends to cause problems later rather than saving time now.
  • Can read Arabic letters but recitation isn't confident or correct yet: Quran Reading with Tajweed is the right next step, focused on pronunciation and the core recitation rules.
  • Already recite comfortably and want to refine the details: Advanced Tajweed focuses on precision, exact articulation and rules that are easy to apply loosely.
  • Want to memorize the Quran, in whole or in part: Quran Memorization (Hifz) is a structured, one-on-one program built around daily new-lesson-plus-revision cycles.
  • Can recite but want to understand what the verses actually mean: Tafseer is discussion-based and works from the Quran text you already read, available in English or Urdu.
  • Want to read the Quran's Arabic directly rather than relying on translation: the Quranic Arabic course builds vocabulary and grammar specific to Quranic, not conversational, Arabic.
  • Want a complete, structured path toward becoming a certified Islamic scholar: the Alim & Aalimah course combines Quran, Tafseer, Hadith, Fiqh and Arabic under one tutor relationship, with a female tutor available throughout for sisters on the Aalimah track.

Still not sure? A free trial class with any course lets your tutor assess your actual level and point you toward the right starting place, there's no wrong door to walk through first.

Not Sure Where to Start?

Message us on WhatsApp and we’ll help you pick the right course and book a free trial class.

Book Free Trial on WhatsApp

Our Mission: The Home of Quran Learning for Every Family

At QuranlyHub, we're the home of Quran learning for busy modern families — bridging the gap between packed schedules and authentic Quranic education. We help students across the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia read Quran online and learn Al Quran online through flexible, personalised, one-to-one classes.✓ Personalised One-to-One Quran Classes✓ Ijazah-Certified Tutors, Teacher Preference on Request✓ Flexible Scheduling for All Time Zones✓ Structured Courses for Kids & Adults Explore Our Courses About Us Our Featured Courses

Early Years Foundation

When Should Children Start Learning the Quran?

Starting Quran education at an early age helps children develop flawless pronunciation skills, deep confidence, and a lifelong connection with the Holy Quran. Many educators consider the early years a valuable window for language and memorisation development. At QuranlyHub, we turn Quran learning into an engaging, interactive and joyful experience through modern digital tools and personalised 1-on-1 attention.

How We Make Learning Engaging for Kids

Interactive Digital Whiteboards

Best Online Quran Classes with Tajweed

Whether you are a parent seeking a solid foundation for your child, or an adult looking to refine your recitation, QuranlyHub offers personalised online Quran classes tailored to your specific pace. Reciting the Holy Quran with proper Tajweed is a responsibility to preserve the Divine Word exactly as it was revealed — our structured classes focus on accuracy, fluency and a lifelong love for the Quran.

Precise articulation points (Makharij) for every Arabic letter, taught with live feedback.

Adults progress through the rules; children thrive on rhythm and repetition — we adapt to both.

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about reading Quran online with QuranlyHub.

How do online Quran classes work?

When you read Quran online with QuranlyHub, classes happen live and one-to-one over video call with an Ijazah-certified tutor, at a time you choose. You’ll need a laptop or tablet, a stable connection and a quiet space — your tutor guides the lesson from there.

What makes QuranlyHub the home of Quran learning online?

QuranlyHub brings every stage of Quran education — Noorani Qaida, Tajweed, Hifz, Tafseer and Quranic Arabic — into one online academy with Ijazah-certified tutors, live 1-on-1 video classes and flexible scheduling for families across the USA, UK, Canada, Australia, UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

Do you have female Quran tutors?

If you have a teacher preference, message us on WhatsApp before your trial and we will do our best to accommodate it. All QuranlyHub tutors are Ijazah-certified in Quran recitation.

How long is the free trial class?

The free trial is a short live session, usually 20 to 30 minutes, used to assess the student’s current level and match them with the right tutor before you choose a plan.

What age groups do you teach?

We teach children from around age 4 through to adults, including reverts with no prior Arabic background. Every course is paced to the individual student, not a fixed age bracket.

Can adults read the Quran online, or is this just for children?

QuranlyHub teaches all ages. Adults can read Quran online from complete beginner level through advanced Tajweed, Hifz and Tafseer, with lessons paced to the individual student rather than a fixed age bracket.

Is an online Quran class the same as an online Koran class?

Yes — ‘Quran’ and ‘Koran’ are two English spellings of the same Holy Book. QuranlyHub’s online Quran classes cover reading, Tajweed, Hifz, Tafseer and Quranic Arabic, all live and one-to-one with Ijazah-certified tutors.

Can I reschedule or cancel a class?

Yes. Message your tutor or QuranlyHub directly on WhatsApp to reschedule or make changes to your classes.

posts.post_title: Learn Tajweed Online: Where Beginners Should Actually Start
posts.post_content:
Short answer: start with the articulation points of the letters (Makharij), not with the named rules. Almost every beginner who struggles with Tajweed started in the wrong place, memorising rule names like Ikhfa and Idgham before they could reliably produce the letters those rules apply to. Get the articulation points right first, and tajweed classes online become far easier to follow.

If you have tried to learn Tajweed online and felt lost, it is very likely a sequencing problem rather than an ability problem. Here is the order that actually works, and roughly how long each stage takes.

What Tajweed actually means

Tajweed is the set of rules governing how the Quran is pronounced: where each letter is formed in the mouth and throat, what qualities it carries, and how letters change when they meet each other. The purpose is preservation. Recited correctly, the text sounds as it was transmitted.

Two practical points beginners often miss. First, Tajweed is a practical skill, not a theoretical subject; you cannot learn it from reading alone, because it depends on a trained ear correcting you. Second, you are already applying much of it before you can name any of it.

Stage 1: Makharij, the articulation points

This is where to begin, and where most self taught learners skip ahead.

Arabic has letters that English does not distinguish. If your haa and haa sound the same, or your seen, saad and thaa collapse into one sound, no amount of rule memorisation will fix the recitation. The rules operate on letters; if the letters are wrong, the rules are decorating an error.

The commonly confused pairs worth drilling early:

  • The two forms of haa, one from the deep throat and one from the middle
  • Seen against saad, and thaa against seen
  • Kaaf against qaaf
  • Taa against taa, and daal against daad
  • Zhaa, dhaal and zaay

Expect this stage to take several weeks. It is slow, it feels unglamorous, and it determines everything after it.

Stage 2: Sifaat, the qualities of letters

Once a letter is coming from the right place, the next layer is how it is produced. Is it heavy or light? Does the sound run or stop? Is there a slight bounce when it carries a sukoon?

This stage is what separates recitation that is technically correct from recitation that sounds right. It is also where a teacher becomes genuinely necessary, because you cannot hear your own heaviness accurately.

Stage 3: The Noon Sakinah and Tanween rules

Now the named rules make sense, because you have the letters to apply them to. There are four, and they cover a large share of what you will meet on any page:

RuleWhat happens
IzharThe noon is pronounced clearly
IdghamThe noon merges into the following letter
IqlabThe noon converts to a meem sound
IkhfaThe noon is partially hidden, with a nasal sound

Learn them by hearing and applying, not by memorising the letter groups first. The groups are a reference, not the lesson.

Stage 4: Madd, the lengthenings

Madd governs how long a vowel is held. Get the natural two count length stable first, then the longer cases. Inconsistent madd is the most audible beginner error, and the easiest to fix once someone points it out.

A realistic timeline

For an adult starting with reasonable reading fluency, attending two to three Tajweed classes online per week:

  • Makharij and correcting confused letters: roughly four to eight weeks
  • Sifaat: another four to six weeks, overlapping
  • Noon Sakinah and Tanween rules: three to four weeks
  • Madd and consolidation: ongoing

Applying it consistently while reciting at normal speed takes considerably longer than learning it. That is normal and not a sign of failure.

Related reading: Tajweed rules are only half the job. See how a Quran recitation course with an Ijazah teacher corrects the sounds you cannot hear yourself.

Already comfortable with the basics and want to check for hidden habits? See our guide on common Tajweed mistakes English speakers make and how to actually fix them.

Already reading fluently and want to refine further? See our guide on advanced Tajweed to check if you are ready for the next level.

New to structured Quran study altogether, not just Tajweed specifically? Our full guide to learning Quran online covers certified tutors, scheduling and what to expect for adults, sisters and kids.

Frequently asked questions

Can I learn Tajweed without a teacher?

You can learn the theory from books and videos. You cannot reliably learn the practice, because Tajweed depends on someone hearing your recitation and correcting it. Self study plus regular correction works well; self study alone tends to embed errors.

Do I need to finish Qaida first?

You need to read Arabic letters and join them. If you are still sounding out individual letters, complete a structured Qaida course first; Tajweed will come much faster afterwards.

How long does an online Tajweed course take?

Most students cover the core rules in three to six months of consistent weekly classes. Fluent application usually takes a year or more.

Is Tajweed obligatory?

Scholars distinguish between the level of Tajweed required to avoid changing meaning, which is considered necessary, and the finer points of beautification, which are recommended. Any qualified teacher can explain this in more detail.

Are tajweed classes online as effective as in-person lessons?

For correction, yes — what matters is a tutor hearing your recitation in real time, which live video delivers just as well as sitting in the same room.

What's the difference between reading Quran online and taking a proper online tajweed course?

Reading Quran online is reciting the text; an online tajweed course teaches the precise pronunciation rules behind that recitation, so mistakes get corrected rather than repeated.

Can I learn tajweed online for free before committing to a course?

Free videos can introduce the concepts, but they can't correct your recitation. Most academies, including QuranlyHub, offer a free trial class instead, which gives you real feedback before you commit to a paid plan.

Starting properly

If you take one thing from this: do not begin with rule names. Begin with the letters. Everything else follows more easily than you expect.

QuranlyHub runs one to one Tajweed courses, structured in exactly this order, with an Advanced Tajweed course to progress into once the basics are solid. Book a free trial class and have your recitation assessed before you commit.

Do I need to know the Arabic alphabet before starting Tajweed?

Yes. Tajweed builds on being able to already read Arabic letters and basic words, typically through completing Noorani Qaida first. Starting Tajweed rules before the alphabet is solid tends to create confusion rather than progress.

What is the very first Tajweed rule a beginner learns?

Makharij al-huroof, the correct articulation points for each letter, comes first, since every other Tajweed rule depends on pronouncing the underlying letters correctly.

posts.post_title: 5 Ways to Keep Kids Motivated in Quran Lessons Online
posts.post_content:
Short answer: children stay motivated in Quran lessons when the sessions are short, the progress is visible, the difficulty is correctly matched, the teacher is warm, and the routine is protected. Motivation is not a personality trait you either have or lack. It is mostly a design problem, and it is fixable. Get this right and children look forward to reading Quran online instead of resisting it.

Every parent who has enrolled a child in online Quran classes for kids knows the pattern. The first fortnight is enthusiastic. By week five there is negotiation, and by week eight there are tears. This is normal, and it usually has less to do with the child than with how the learning is structured.

1. Make the sessions shorter than you think they should be

The most common mistake is buying long lessons because they feel like better value. For a child aged five to nine, focused attention on a demanding task tends to run out well before the half hour mark, and pushing past that point mostly teaches the child that Quran time is when they feel tired and corrected.

Thirty minutes, four times a week, will almost always beat an hour twice a week. The child finishes while still able to concentrate, which is the feeling you want them to associate with the lesson.

2. Make progress visible

Adults can hold an abstract goal in mind for months. Children cannot. If the only marker of progress is finishing the Quran one day, there is nothing to feel good about this week.

Give the progress a physical or visual form:

  • A wall chart with a sticker for every completed lesson.
  • A short recording of their recitation once a month, so they can hear the difference themselves.
  • A simple certificate when they finish Qaida and move to the Quran.

Hearing their own recitation from three months ago is often the single most motivating thing a child experiences.

3. Check the difficulty is actually right

What looks like laziness is very often mismatch. A child who is bored and a child who is overwhelmed produce identical behaviour: avoidance.

The rough test is the accuracy of the first attempt. If they recite a new line correctly almost every time, it is too easy and they are coasting. If they stumble on most of it, it is too hard and they are guessing. Somewhere in between is where learning feels satisfying.

Ask the teacher to adjust deliberately. Good quran classes for beginners should move in small, well judged steps rather than fixed weekly quotas.

4. The teacher relationship carries more weight than the curriculum

Children work hard for teachers they like. This is not sentimentality; it is how children are built.

Watch how the tutor handles a mistake. Do they correct the letter, or does the child feel corrected as a person? Do they use the child's name? Do they ever laugh? A tutor who is technically excellent but cold will produce a child who recites accurately and quietly resents it.

If your child dreads the class after a fair trial period, ask to change teacher before you conclude your child dislikes the Quran. Those are different problems.

5. Protect the routine, and keep parents out of the correcting role

Same time, same place, same days. A fixed slot removes the daily negotiation, and the negotiation is what exhausts everyone.

One caution worth stating plainly: try not to become the second teacher. When a parent corrects pronunciation at home on top of the lesson, the child ends up with no space where Quran is simply enjoyable. Read together, listen together, ask what they learned. Leave the corrections to the tutor.

What normal progress looks like

StageTypical focusWhat to expect
Starting outLetter recognition and soundsSlow, repetitive, easy to underestimate
Joining lettersWords and short versesNoticeable jump in confidence
Reading QuranFluency with basic TajweedProgress feels faster to the child

Plateaus are part of this, particularly in the first stage. They are not a sign the child cannot do it.

Working with an older child specifically? See our guide on online Quran classes for teenagers, the motivation strategies that work for younger kids often backfire at this age.

Not sure what to expect at your child's specific age? See our guide on online Quran classes for kids by age.

Frequently asked questions

What age should a child start Quran lessons?

Around four to six works well for most children, once they can sit and focus for a short period. Starting later is not a disadvantage; older children usually progress through the alphabet faster.

How long should a Quran lesson be for a young child?

About thirty minutes. Shorter and more frequent beats longer and rarer, almost always.

My child was keen and now refuses. What do I do?

Check difficulty first, then the teacher relationship, then the schedule. In that order. Reducing lesson length temporarily often resolves it without any other change.

Do rewards spoil the intention?

Small markers of encouragement help a young child build the habit. As they mature, the motivation naturally shifts inward. Most teachers see this as scaffolding, not bribery.

Does reading Quran online instead of in person affect a child's motivation?

Not inherently. What affects motivation is session length, visible progress, and the teacher relationship, not the format. Many children focus better online since there is no travel to add fatigue before the lesson even starts.

How do I know if my child is ready for online quran classes for beginners?

If they can sit and focus for roughly the length of the lesson, they're ready. Reading ability isn't a prerequisite, since beginner courses start from the alphabet itself.

Can motivation problems mean the course is too advanced?

Yes, this is one of the most common causes. A tutor can reassess level in a single session and adjust the pace, often resolving what looks like a motivation problem within a week or two.

Getting the setup right

Motivation follows a good structure. Short sessions, visible progress, correct difficulty, a warm teacher and a protected routine will carry a child further than any amount of encouragement.

At QuranlyHub, lessons are one to one and scheduled around your family's routine. See our courses for kids or book a free trial class.

How do I keep my child motivated for Quran lessons long-term?

Short, consistent sessions with visible small wins (finishing a lesson, reading a new word correctly) tend to sustain motivation better than long sessions or rigid, joyless drilling. A tutor who genuinely connects with the child also makes a bigger difference than any specific technique.

Should I reward my child for completing Quran lessons?

Small, occasional rewards can help early motivation, but building genuine enjoyment of the lessons themselves (through a patient, encouraging tutor) tends to sustain motivation longer than a reward system alone.

posts.post_title: Best Online Quran Academy: How to Choose the Right Teacher
posts.post_content:
Short answer: choosing an online Quran teacher comes down to six things you can verify before you pay anything: their certification, how they handle absolute beginners, whether they can match your gender preference, what actually happens in the trial class, how they report progress, and whether their timetable genuinely fits your week. Everything else is marketing. Get these right and you can read Quran online with confidence that you picked the right academy, not just the best marketing.

Most families searching for online Quran classes start by comparing prices. That is the wrong first filter. The gap between a good and a poor teacher shows up in whether your child still wants to attend after eight weeks, and price tells you almost nothing about that. Here is what to look at instead.

1. Ask what "certified" actually means

The word certified is used loosely. Ask directly: does the teacher hold an Ijazah, and in which recitation? An Ijazah is a formal authorisation showing the teacher recited the Quran to a qualified scholar who confirmed their accuracy, in an unbroken chain of transmission. It is the closest thing to a verifiable teaching credential in this field.

A serious online Quran academy will answer this plainly. If the reply is vague, treat that as information.

2. Ask how they teach someone who knows nothing

Teaching a fluent reader is easy. Teaching a five year old, or an adult revert who has never seen the Arabic alphabet, is the real test.

Good answers sound specific: they start with letter recognition and articulation points before joining letters, they use Noorani Qaida or a comparable structured method, and they do not move on until the student is consistent. Vague answers about going at your pace usually mean there is no method at all.

3. Decide the gender question early

Many families want a female Quran teacher online, particularly for sisters and young girls, and there is nothing awkward about asking. A well staffed academy will have qualified female tutors available and will not treat the request as unusual. Ask before the trial, not after.

4. Treat the trial class as an interview

Almost every provider offers free Quran classes as a trial. Use it properly. In that first session, notice:

  • Does the teacher assess the student's current level, or launch straight into a lesson?
  • Do they correct pronunciation gently and specifically, or let mistakes pass?
  • Does the student speak and recite, or mostly listen?
  • Is the audio clear and the connection stable?

A trial where the student barely recites tells you very little. Ask the teacher to have them read aloud.

5. Ask what progress reporting looks like

This is where many providers quietly fail. You should know, without chasing anyone, what was covered last month and what comes next. Ask to see an example report. Keeping you updated is not a system.

6. Check the schedule honestly

Time zones decide whether this lasts. If you are in London, New York, Toronto or Sydney, confirm the exact local slot in writing, and ask what happens when a class is missed. A clear reschedule policy matters more than an extra discount.

Red flags worth walking away from

  • No named teacher before you pay.
  • Pressure to commit to six or twelve months upfront.
  • Reviews that all sound identical and appear in the same week.
  • No written policy for cancellation or refunds.
  • Reluctance to answer the Ijazah question directly.

Questions to ask before you enrol

Copy these into your trial booking message:

  1. Which teacher will my child have, and what is their qualification?
  2. Will it be the same teacher every week?
  3. What curriculum do you follow for beginners?
  4. How and when will I receive progress updates?
  5. What is your rescheduling and cancellation policy?

Frequently asked questions

How long should a trial class be?

Twenty to thirty minutes is normal. That is long enough to assess level and see teaching style, and short enough that a young child stays engaged.

Is one-to-one really better than group classes?

For recitation, yes. Tajweed correction depends on the teacher hearing each letter clearly, which is difficult in a group. Group formats can work for theory, but not for correcting pronunciation.

How often should classes be to see progress?

Two to four sessions a week is the range most students settle into. Consistency matters more than session length; four short lessons beat one long one.

Can adults start from zero?

Yes, and many do. Adults often move through the alphabet faster than children because they understand the rules conceptually, though they may need more repetition for fluency.

What's the difference between choosing a teacher and choosing the best online quran academy?

A good individual teacher matters, but the academy around them matters too — how trials are run, how progress is reported, and what happens if a tutor is unavailable. The best online quran academy gets both right, not just the teacher.

Should I pick a teacher whose style matches how I want to read Quran online?

It helps to hear their recitation style in the trial, but accuracy and clarity matter more than personal style at the early stages. Style differences narrow once the fundamentals are solid.

Is it worth switching teachers if progress feels slow?

Sometimes, but rule out schedule and difficulty-level mismatches first. A tutor change is a bigger disruption than adjusting pace or frequency, so try the smaller fix before the bigger one.

What makes one online Quran academy better than another?

Tutor qualifications (Ijazah, experience), one-to-one versus group format, whether the academy assesses your level before starting, availability of female teachers, transparent pricing, and a genuine free trial are the factors that actually predict a good experience, more than marketing claims.

Should I trust online reviews when choosing a Quran academy?

Reviews are useful context but a free trial class is more reliable, since it lets you personally judge the specific tutor's teaching style and whether it suits your or your child's learning needs before committing.
